title: Kingdom of Romania
capsule: The Kingdom of Romania (Regatul României) was the constitutional monarchy that emerged from Greater Romania after World War I — its 1919 borders, confirmed by the Treaty of Versailles and Treaty of Trianon (1920), incorporated Transylvania, Bessarabia, and Bukovina, roughly doubling the pre-war state. Under King Ferdinand I (r. 1914–1927) and his successors Carol II (r. 1930–1940) and Mihai I, Romania navigated interwar instability, territorial losses to the Soviet Union and Hungary in 1940 under the Ribbentrop-Molotov Pact and the Vienna Award, then re-entered the war on the Axis side before switching to the Allies in August 1944. Soviet occupation and communist consolidation followed; on 30 December 1947 King Mihai I was forced to abdicate, and the Romanian People's Republic was proclaimed, ending the monarchy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries are well documented through successive peace treaties; the 1940 territorial changes are precisely recorded, and the state's geographic extent at each phase is well established in modern historiography.
